## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# 1. Read in the edgeR tsv file
# The file uses standard tab separation
diff_acc_data <- read_tsv("/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/comparison1_diffacc_edgeR.tsv")

# 2. Define thresholds for differential accessibility
# Adjust these thresholds based on your experimental design
fdr_threshold <- 0.05
logfc_threshold <- 1.0

# 3. Classify peaks into Open (ctrl), Closed (A485), or Non-Significant
plot_data <- diff_acc_data %>%
  mutate(
    Significance = case_when(
      FDR < fdr_threshold & logFC > logfc_threshold  ~ "Enriched in Ctrl",
      FDR < fdr_threshold & logFC < -logfc_threshold ~ "Enriched in A485",
      TRUE                                           ~ "Not Significant"
    )
  )

# Count how many peaks fall into each category
print(table(plot_data$Significance))

# 4. Generate the enhanced MA Plot
ma_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = logCPM, y = logFC)) +
  # Use geom_point with alpha blending to handle high-density overlapping points
  geom_point(aes(color = Significance), size = 1.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Add horizontal helper lines for your logFC thresholds
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-logfc_threshold, logfc_threshold), 
             linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black", size = 0.6) +
  
  # Custom color palette matching your condition groups
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Enriched in Ctrl" = "#de2d26",   # Red
      "Enriched in A485" = "#3182bd",   # Blue
      "Not Significant"  = "#969696"    # Muted Gray
    )
  ) +
  
  # Clean, publication-ready theme
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  
  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "MA Plot: Differential Chromatin Accessibility",
    x = "Average Abundance (logCPM)",
    y = "Log Fold Change (logFC)",
    color = "Status"
  )

# Display the plot
print(ma_plot)

# Optional: Save the plot to a high-res file
# ggsave("fixed_ma_plot.png", plot = ma_plot, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# 1. Read in the edgeR output file
df <- read_tsv("/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/comparison1_diffacc_edgeR.tsv")

# 2. Define significance status based on FDR threshold (< 0.05)
# This prevents the non-significant points from splitting into groups at y = 0
df <- df %>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
    FDR < 0.05 & logFC > 0 ~ "Enriched in ctrl",
    FDR < 0.05 & logFC < 0 ~ "Enriched in A485",
    TRUE                   ~ "Not Significant"
  ))

# Define a consistent color palette
group_colors <- c(
  "Enriched in ctrl" = "#de2d26",   # Red
  "Enriched in A485" = "#3182bd",   # Blue
  "Not Significant"  = "#d9d9d9"    # Muted light gray
)

# ==========================================
# Plot 1: Corrected MA Plot
# ==========================================
ma_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = logCPM, y = logFC, color = Status)) +
  # Plot background non-significant points first, then overlay significant ones
  geom_point(data = filter(df, Status == "Not Significant"), alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = filter(df, Status != "Not Significant"), alpha = 0.9, size = 1.5) +
  
  # Horizontal reference baseline
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Differential Chromatin Accessibility (Corrected)",
    subtitle = "Highlighted peaks pass FDR < 0.05",
    x = "Average Abundance (logCPM)",
    y = "Log2 Fold Change (logFC)",
    color = "Significance Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(ma_plot)

# ==========================================
# Plot 2: Bar Chart of Enriched Counts
# ==========================================
# Filter out non-significant peaks and count totals
count_data <- df %>%
  filter(Status != "Not Significant") %>%
  count(Status)

bar_plot <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = Status, y = n, fill = Status)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.5, color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  # Add text labels on top of each bar
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 5) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Significantly Enriched Peaks",
    subtitle = "Threshold: FDR < 0.05",
    x = "Experimental Group",
    y = "Peak Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none" # Hide legend since x-axis labels identify groups
  ) +
  # Expand y-axis limits slightly to ensure text labels aren't cut off
  ylim(0, max(count_data$n) * 1.15)

print(bar_plot)

# Optional: Save both plots to high-resolution PNGs
# ggsave("corrected_ma_plot.png", plot = ma_plot, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
# ggsave("enriched_counts_bar.png", plot = bar_plot, width = 5, height = 5, dpi = 300)

```
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# 1. Read in the edgeR output file
df <- read_tsv("/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/comparison1_diffacc_edgeR.tsv")

# 2. Define significance status based on FDR threshold (< 0.05)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
    FDR < 0.05 & logFC > 0 ~ "Enriched in ctrl",
    FDR < 0.05 & logFC < 0 ~ "Enriched in A485",
    TRUE                   ~ "Not Significant"
  ))

# 3. Dynamically count the number of peaks in each group for the labels
counts <- table(df$Status)
label_ctrl  <- paste0("Enriched in ctrl (", counts["Enriched in ctrl"], ")")
label_a485  <- paste0("Enriched in A485 (", counts["Enriched in A485"], ")")
label_nosig <- paste0("Not Significant (", counts["Not Significant"], ")")

# 4. Define the color palette mapping directly to the new dynamic labels
group_colors <- c(
  "Enriched in ctrl" = "#de2d26",   # Red
  "Enriched in A485" = "#3182bd",   # Blue
  "Not Significant"  = "#d9d9d9"    # Muted light gray
)

# Replace status strings with the ones containing parenthetical counts
df <- df %>%
  mutate(Status_Label = case_when(
    Status == "Enriched in ctrl" ~ label_ctrl,
    Status == "Enriched in A485" ~ label_a485,
    TRUE                         ~ label_nosig
  ))

# Create a named vector for the scale mapping using the exact label strings
color_labels <- c(group_colors["Enriched in ctrl"], 
                  group_colors["Enriched in A485"], 
                  group_colors["Not Significant"])
names(color_labels) <- c(label_ctrl, label_a485, label_nosig)


# ==========================================
# Plot 1: Corrected MA Plot with Dynamic Labels
# ==========================================
ma_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = logCPM, y = logFC, color = Status_Label)) +
  # Render non-significant background points first
  geom_point(data = filter(df, Status == "Not Significant"), alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  # Overlay the significant points on top
  geom_point(data = filter(df, Status != "Not Significant"), alpha = 0.9, size = 1.5) +
  
  # Reference line at y = 0
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = color_labels) +
  labs(
    title = "Differential Chromatin Accessibility",
    subtitle = "Statistical Significance Threshold: FDR < 0.05",
    x = "Average Abundance (logCPM)",
    y = "Log2 Fold Change (logFC)",
    color = "Significance Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(ma_plot)


# ==========================================
# Plot 2: Bar Chart of Enriched Counts with Dynamic Labels
# ==========================================
# Filter out non-significant peaks for the bar chart
count_data <- df %>%
  filter(Status != "Not Significant") %>%
  count(Status_Label)

bar_plot <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = Status_Label, y = n, fill = Status_Label)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.5, color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 5) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_labels) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Significantly Enriched Peaks",
    subtitle = "Threshold: FDR < 0.05",
    x = "Experimental Group",
    y = "Peak Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  ylim(0, max(count_data$n) * 1.15)

print(bar_plot)
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Read in the edgeR output file
df <- read_tsv("/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/comparison1_diffacc_edgeR.tsv")

# 2. Extract coordinates from peak_id and filter for significant up-peaks
# True significant up-peaks are determined by FDR < 0.05
coords_df <- df %>%
  filter(FDR < 0.05) %>%
  separate(
    col = peak_id, 
    into = c("chr", "start", "end"), 
    sep = "\\|", 
    convert = TRUE
  ) %>%
  # Ensure chromosomes are properly named (e.g., "chr9" or "chrJH584304.1")
  mutate(chr = if_else(grepl("^chr", chr), chr, paste0("chr", chr)))

# 3. Separate by group assignment and select just the coordinate columns
# Group 1: Significant up-peaks in ctrl
ctrl_up_peaks <- coords_df %>%
  filter(logFC > 0) %>%
  select(chr, start, end, logFC, FDR)

# Group 2: Significant up-peaks in A485
a485_up_peaks <- coords_df %>%
  filter(logFC < 0) %>%
  select(chr, start, end, logFC, FDR)

# 4. Print summaries to console
cat("Extracted", nrow(ctrl_up_peaks), "coordinates for ctrl group.\n")
cat("Extracted", nrow(a485_up_peaks), "coordinates for A485 group.\n")

# 5. Save the separated coordinates to files
# Standard tab-separated summary files
write_tsv(ctrl_up_peaks, "/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/ctrl_up_peaks_coordinates.tsv")
write_tsv(a485_up_peaks, "/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/a485_up_peaks_coordinates.tsv")

# Optional: Save in standard 3-column BED format for downstream tools (like IGV, MEME, or bedtools)
write_tsv(ctrl_up_peaks %>% select(chr, start, end), "/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/ctrl_up_peaks.bed", col_names = FALSE)
write_tsv(a485_up_peaks %>% select(chr, start, end), "/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/a485_up_peaks.bed", col_names = FALSE)

```
#Do some pathway analysis
```{r}
# Install required Bioconductor packages if you don't have them:
# BiocManager::install(c("ChIPseeker", "clusterProfiler", "TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene", "org.Mm.eg.db"))

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ChIPseeker)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. READ DATA & CONVERT TO GENOMIC RANGES (GRanges)
# ==============================================================================
# Read the edgeR file
df <- read_tsv("/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison2/comparison2_diffacc_edgeR.tsv")

# Separate peak_id coordinates and fix chromosome names
processed_df <- df %>%
  separate(col = peak_id, into = c("chr", "start", "end"), sep = "\\|", convert = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(chr = if_else(grepl("^chr", chr), chr, paste0("chr", chr)))

# Filter specifically for the significantly up-regulated peaks in A485
# (FDR < 0.05 and logFC < 0 means more accessible/enriched in A485)
a485_peaks_df <- processed_df %>%
  filter(FDR < 0.05 & logFC < 0)

# Convert the dataframe to a GRanges object required by ChIPseeker
a485_granges <- GRanges(
  seqnames = a485_peaks_df$chr,
  ranges = IRanges(start = a485_peaks_df$start, end = a485_peaks_df$end),
  logFC = a485_peaks_df$logFC,
  FDR = a485_peaks_df$FDR
)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. PEAK ANNOTATION (Finding Nearest Genes)
# ==============================================================================
# Load the genomic database (Change to hg38 for human)
txdb <- TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene

# Annotate peaks (assigns genomic feature like Promoter, Exon, Intron, Intergenic)
# and calculates exact distance to the nearest Transcription Start Site (TSS)
a485_annotated <- annotatePeak(
  a485_granges, 
  tssRegion = c(-3000, 3000), # Define promoter region window
  TxDb = txdb, 
  annoDb = "org.Mm.eg.db"       # Provides official gene symbols
)

# Convert annotation results back to a standard dataframe
a485_anno_df <- as.data.frame(a485_annotated)

# Save the full peak annotation report
write_tsv(a485_anno_df, "/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison2/A485_peaks_annotated_genes.tsv")

# View a breakdown of genomic features (e.g., % in promoters vs intergenic)
print(head(a485_anno_df[, c("seqnames", "start", "end", "annotation", "distanceToTSS", "SYMBOL")]))

# Plot the distribution of features
plotAnnoBar(a485_annotated)


# ==============================================================================
# 3. PATHWAY ENRICHMENT ANALYSIS (KEGG)
# ==============================================================================
# Extract unique Entrez Gene IDs associated with your A485 peaks
# ClusterProfiler works best using numerical Entrez IDs
target_genes <- unique(a485_anno_df$geneId)

# Run KEGG Over-Representation Analysis
# (Change organism = "hsa" if you are using human data)
kegg_enrichment <- enrichKEGG(
  gene          = target_genes,
  organism      = "mmu", 
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff  = 0.2
)

# Translate Entrez IDs in the output pathways back to human-readable Gene Symbols
kegg_enrichment <- setReadable(kegg_enrichment, OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID")

# Save pathway analysis results table
write_tsv(as.data.frame(kegg_enrichment), "A485_kegg_pathways.tsv")

# ==============================================================================
# 4. VISUALIZE PATHWAY RESULTS
# ==============================================================================
# 1. Standard Dotplot: Shows enrichment score (GeneRatio) and significance (p.adjust)
kegg_dotplot <- dotplot(kegg_enrichment, showCategory = 15) + 
  ggtitle("KEGG Pathways - Enriched in A485")
print(kegg_dotplot)

# 2. Category-Gene Network Plot (cnetplot): Shows which specific genes belong to which pathway
kegg_cnet <- cnetplot(kegg_enrichment, categorySize = "pvalue", foldChange = NULL, circular = FALSE) +
  ggtitle("Gene-Pathway Network Mapping")
print(kegg_cnet)
```

#Integrate with the RNAseq data
```{r}
# Ensure you have the necessary libraries installed:
# BiocManager::install(c("ChIPseeker", "TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene", "org.Mm.eg.db"))
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "ggrepel"))

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ChIPseeker)
library(TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOAD AND ANNOTATE ATAC-SEQ PEAKS
# ==============================================================================
# Read in the ATAC-seq edgeR file provided previously
atac_df <- read_tsv("/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison1/comparison1_diffacc_edgeR.tsv")

# Parse coordinates and standardize chromosome names
atac_processed <- atac_df %>%
  separate(col = peak_id, into = c("chr", "start", "end"), sep = "\\|", convert = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(chr = if_else(grepl("^chr", chr), chr, paste0("chr", chr)))

# Convert to GRanges object
atac_granges <- GRanges(
  seqnames = atac_processed$chr,
  ranges = IRanges(start = atac_processed$start, end = atac_processed$end),
  atac_logFC = atac_processed$logFC,
  atac_FDR = atac_processed$FDR
)

# Annotate peaks with closest genes using mouse genome annotation (change to hg38 if human)
txdb <- TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene
atac_annotated <- annotatePeak(atac_granges, tssRegion = c(-3000, 3000), 
                               TxDb = txdb, annoDb = "org.Mm.eg.db")

# Convert back to data frame and keep relevant columns
#atac_annotated_df <- as.data.frame(atac_annotated) %>%
#  select(SYMBOL, atac_logFC, atac_FDR, distanceToTSS, annotation)
atac_annotated_df <- as.data.frame(atac_annotated) %>%
  dplyr::select(SYMBOL, atac_logFC, atac_FDR, distanceToTSS, annotation)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. LOAD DESEQ2 RNA-SEQ DATA AND INTEGRATE
# ==============================================================================
# Read in your DESeq2 output file
# The first column with Ensembl IDs lacks a header string name in standard DESeq2 TSVs, 
# but read_tsv handles this automatically or skips it if we don't explicitly select it.
#rna_raw <- read_tsv("/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/RNAseq/DESeq2_SampleSheet_RNAseq/DEseq_basic_DEresults.tsv") 

deseq_col_names <- c("ensembl_id", "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", 
                     "stat", "pvalue", "padj", "Status", "external_gene_name")
rna_raw <- read_tsv(
  "/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/RNAseq/DESeq2_SampleSheet_RNAseq/DEseq_basic_DEresults.tsv",
  skip = 1, 
  col_names = deseq_col_names
)

# Clean DESeq2 data and map to standardized column names
rna_df <- rna_raw %>%
  # Remove rows with NA values for statistics
  filter(!is.na(padj) & !is.na(log2FoldChange)) %>% 
  # Select and rename columns to standardize with the ATAC pipeline
  dplyr::select(
    SYMBOL = external_gene_name,
    rna_logFC = log2FoldChange,
    rna_FDR = padj
  )

# Verify the alignment fix
print("Verified Cleaned RNA-Seq Data:")
print(head(rna_df))

# Preview the repaired data frame to make sure it looks right
print("Repaired RNA Data Sample:")
print(head(rna_df))
# Merge the datasets by official Gene Symbol
# We filter for peaks close to promoters/genes (e.g., within 5kb of TSS) to focus on direct regulation
integrated_df <- inner_join(atac_annotated_df, rna_df, by = "SYMBOL") %>%
  filter(abs(distanceToTSS) <= 5000)

# Classify the integration groups for visualization thresholds (FDR < 0.05)
integrated_df <- integrated_df %>%
  mutate(Regulation = case_when(
    atac_FDR < 0.05 & rna_FDR < 0.05 & atac_logFC > 0 & rna_logFC > 0 ~ "Co-upregulated (Open & Expressed)",
    atac_FDR < 0.05 & rna_FDR < 0.05 & atac_logFC < 0 & rna_logFC < 0 ~ "Co-downregulated (Closed & Silenced)",
    atac_FDR < 0.05 & rna_FDR < 0.05                                  ~ "Inverse Regulation",
    TRUE                                                               ~ "Not Concordant / Not Sig"
  ))

# Save the integrated table
write_tsv(integrated_df, "integrated_atac_rna_summary.tsv")

# ==============================================================================
# 3. VISUALIZATION: STARBURST PLOT
# ==============================================================================
# Color scheme matching biological context
integration_colors <- c(
  "Co-upregulated (Open & Expressed)"   = "#de2d26", # Red
  "Co-downregulated (Closed & Silenced)" = "#3182bd", # Blue
  "Inverse Regulation"                   = "#74c476", # Green
  "Not Concordant / Not Sig"             = "#d9d9d9"  # Muted gray
)

starburst_plot <- ggplot(integrated_df, aes(x = atac_logFC, y = rna_logFC)) +
  # Plot non-significant/non-concordant markers in background
  geom_point(data = filter(integrated_df, Regulation == "Not Concordant / Not Sig"), 
             alpha = 0.3, size = 1, color = "#d9d9d9") +
  # Overlay significant, multi-omic hits
  geom_point(data = filter(integrated_df, Regulation != "Not Concordant / Not Sig"), 
             aes(color = Regulation), alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
  
  # Add crosshair lines at 0
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Dynamically label top multi-omic genes (highest fold changes)
  geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(integrated_df, Regulation != "Not Concordant / Not Sig" & 
                   (abs(atac_logFC) > 1 | abs(rna_logFC) > 1)),
    aes(label = SYMBOL),
    size = 3.5,
    max.overlaps = 15,
    fontface = "bold",
    box.padding = 0.3
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = integration_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Multi-Omic Integration: ATAC-seq vs. RNA-seq",
    subtitle = "Peaks restricted within 5kb of target Gene TSS",
    x = "Chromatin Accessibility Change (ATAC-seq logFC)",
    y = "Gene Expression Change (DESeq2 log2FoldChange)",
    color = "Integration Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(starburst_plot)

# Save high-res plot
# ggsave("atac_rna_starburst_plot.png", plot = starburst_plot, width = 8, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ChIPseeker)
library(TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOAD AND ANNOTATE ATAC-SEQ PEAKS
# ==============================================================================
atac_df <- read_tsv("/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/bams_Project_3969_pseudoreplicates_AOS_0.13/twogroup/comparison2/comparison2_diffacc_edgeR.tsv")

atac_processed <- atac_df %>%
  separate(col = peak_id, into = c("chr", "start", "end"), sep = "\\|", convert = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(chr = if_else(grepl("^chr", chr), chr, paste0("chr", chr)))

atac_granges <- GRanges(
  seqnames = atac_processed$chr,
  ranges = IRanges(start = atac_processed$start, end = atac_processed$end),
  atac_logFC = atac_processed$logFC,
  atac_FDR = atac_processed$FDR
)

txdb <- TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene
atac_annotated <- annotatePeak(atac_granges, tssRegion = c(-3000, 3000), 
                               TxDb = txdb, annoDb = "org.Mm.eg.db")

atac_annotated_df <- as.data.frame(atac_annotated) %>%
  dplyr::select(SYMBOL, atac_logFC, atac_FDR, distanceToTSS, annotation)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. LOAD DESEQ2 RNA-SEQ DATA AND INTEGRATE
# ==============================================================================
deseq_col_names <- c("ensembl_id", "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", 
                     "stat", "pvalue", "padj", "Status", "external_gene_name")
rna_raw <- read_tsv(
  "/data/jenuwein/erikson/2026/ulATAC/RNAseq/v1_DESeq2_SampleSheet_RNAseq/DEseq_basic_DEresults.tsv",
  skip = 1, 
  col_names = deseq_col_names
)

rna_df <- rna_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj) & !is.na(log2FoldChange)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    SYMBOL = external_gene_name,
    rna_logFC = log2FoldChange,
    rna_FDR = padj
  )

# Merge datasets by official Gene Symbol and filter for proximal promoter/TSS hits (<= 5kb)
integrated_df <- inner_join(atac_annotated_df, rna_df, by = "SYMBOL") %>%
  filter(abs(distanceToTSS) <= 5000)

# Step A: Initially assign the baseline statuses
integrated_df <- integrated_df %>%
  mutate(Status_Base = case_when(
    atac_FDR < 0.05 & rna_FDR < 0.05 & atac_logFC > 0 & rna_logFC > 0 ~ "Co-upregulated (Open & Expressed)",
    atac_FDR < 0.05 & rna_FDR < 0.05 & atac_logFC < 0 & rna_logFC < 0 ~ "Co-downregulated (Closed & Silenced)",
    atac_FDR < 0.05 & rna_FDR < 0.05                                  ~ "Inverse Regulation",
    TRUE                                                               ~ "Not Concordant / Not Sig"
  ))

# Step B: Compute the unique counts for each category safely
counts <- table(integrated_df$Status_Base)

# Step C: Generate text labels containing the parenthetical count values
# (Using dynamic lookup to default to 0 if a group happens to have no elements)
get_count <- function(name) if (name %in% names(counts)) counts[name] else 0

label_coup   <- paste0("Co-upregulated (Open & Expressed) (", get_count("Co-upregulated (Open & Expressed)"), ")")
label_codown <- paste0("Co-downregulated (Closed & Silenced) (", get_count("Co-downregulated (Closed & Silenced)"), ")")
label_inv    <- paste0("Inverse Regulation (", get_count("Inverse Regulation"), ")")
label_nosig  <- paste0("Not Concordant / Not Sig (", get_count("Not Concordant / Not Sig"), ")")

# Step D: Apply the finalized text strings with counts into a new variable column
integrated_df <- integrated_df %>%
  mutate(Regulation_Label = case_when(
    Status_Base == "Co-upregulated (Open & Expressed)"   ~ label_coup,
    Status_Base == "Co-downregulated (Closed & Silenced)" ~ label_codown,
    Status_Base == "Inverse Regulation"                   ~ label_inv,
    TRUE                                                   ~ label_nosig
  ))

# Save the updated table summary
write_tsv(integrated_df, "integrated_atac_rna_summary.tsv")


# ==============================================================================
# 3. VISUALIZATION: STARBURST PLOT WITH DYNAMIC LABELS
# ==============================================================================
# Build custom hex color palettes mapped exactly to the explicit new text labels
integration_colors <- c(
  "#74c476", # Green
  "#3182bd", # Blue
  "#de2d26", # Red
  "#d9d9d9"  # Muted light gray
)
names(integration_colors) <- c(label_coup, label_codown, label_inv, label_nosig)

starburst_plot <- ggplot(integrated_df, aes(x = atac_logFC, y = rna_logFC)) +
  # 1. Render non-significant/non-concordant background points first
  geom_point(data = filter(integrated_df, Status_Base == "Not Concordant / Not Sig"), 
             alpha = 0.3, size = 1, color = "#d9d9d9") +
  # 2. Overlay significant integrated multi-omic targets on top
  geom_point(data = filter(integrated_df, Status_Base != "Not Concordant / Not Sig"), 
             aes(color = Regulation_Label), alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
  
  # Crosshair lines at 0 coordinates
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Label top multi-omic genes (highest fold shifts)
  geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(integrated_df, Status_Base != "Not Concordant / Not Sig" & 
                   (abs(atac_logFC) > 1 | abs(rna_logFC) > 1)),
    aes(label = SYMBOL),
    size = 3.5,
    max.overlaps = 15,
    fontface = "bold",
    box.padding = 0.3
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = integration_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "ATAC-seq vs. RNA-seq",
    subtitle = "Peaks restricted within 5kb of target Gene TSS",
    x = "Chromatin Accessibility Change (ATAC-seq logFC)",
    y = "Gene Expression Change (DESeq2 log2FoldChange)",
    color = "Integration Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(starburst_plot)

```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
